ground_truth: Describes the upper bound rate of growth of an algorithm's execution time or memory as input size N grows toward infinity.
pre_quiz: What does O(N) mean when the input size doubles?
pre_quiz_answer: The execution operations or running time also approximately doubles.
post_quiz: Why is an O(N log N) algorithm preferred over an O(N^2) algorithm for large data?
post_quiz_answer: Because N log N scales much slower than quadratic N^2 as N grows into thousands or millions.
